input.title: A question of attribution: Shah v HSBC Private Bank (UK) Ltd [2011] EWCA Civ 1154
input.abstract: In the latest instalment of this long running litigation, the Court of Appeal has given a clear steer on whose state of mind is to be attributed to a bank where a bank suspects money laundering and has frozen a customer's account. The Court observed that it is the bank's 'nominated officer' under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (who makes the report toSOCA) who constitutes the bank for the purposes of the bank itself having the relevant suspicion. The Court did not envisage that banks will call employees further down the reporting chain and held that, in the absence of evidence of bad faith, the duty of standard disclosure did not require the bank to reveal the names of those employees.

output.reasoning: O artigo não atende aos critérios básicos de busca por palavras-chave do protocolo (métodos computacionais, lavagem de dinheiro ou crime organizado) nos campos de título, resumo ou palavras-chave dos autores.
